'''''Potentilla recta''''', the '''sulphur cinquefoil'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PORE5|taxon=Potentilla recta|accessdate=13 October 2015}}</ref>  or '''rough-fruited cinquefoil''', is a species of [[Potentilla|cinquefoil]]. It is native to Eurasia but it is present in [[North America]] as an [[introduced species]], ranging through almost the entire continent except the northernmost part of [[Canada]] and [[Alaska]].

The plant probably originated in the [[Mediterranean Basin]]. In North America, it was first collected in the 19th century in [[Ontario]] and in 1914 in [[British Columbia]].<ref name=fs>{{cite web |title=SPECIES: Potentilla recta |url=http://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/forb/potrec/all.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220213082120/http://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/forb/potrec/all.html |publisher=US Forest Service Fire Ecology |archive-date=2022-02-13 }}</ref> It is known as a minor [[noxious weed]] in some areas.<ref name=fs/> It occurs in many types of habitat, including disturbed, weedy places.

==Description==
Sulphur cinquefoil is a perennial herb and is a tufted plant growing from a woody [[taproot]] or [[caudex]]. It produces upright to erect leafy stems up to {{convert|80|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall. The upper part of the stem is branched and densely hairy, and it also bears some glandular hairs. The lower leaves have long stalks and the stem leaves are arranged alternately and have short stalks. All the leaves are palmate, divided into usually six or seven leaflets, sometimes up to nine, with the uppermost ones just having three leaflets. The green to yellow-green leaves may be up to {{convert|15|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, with the central leaflet reaching {{convert|8|cm|1|abbr=on}} in length. The leaflets are linear-lanceolate, hairy in texture and toothed along the edges. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[Cyme (botany)|cyme]] of several flowers which are generally light to pale yellow in color, with white to gold-flowered individuals occurring at times. Each flower has five [[Sepal|calyx]] lobes, five broad, shallowly-notched [[petal]]s, thirty [[stamen]]s, many [[pistil]]s and a separate [[gynoecium]]. The fruit is a receptacle containing several glossy, pale brown [[achene]]s. The plant may reproduce by seed or [[vegetative reproduction|vegetatively]] by sprouting new shoots from its caudex. Sulphur cinquefoil flowers from June to August.<ref name=fs/><ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/sulphur-cinquefoil |title=Sulphur cinquefoil: ''Potentilla recta'' |publisher=NatureGate |accessdate=2013-12-30}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Sulphur cinquefoil is native to much of Europe, Asia, and parts of North America, and it can be found in other parts of the world as an introduced species.<ref name=fs/> Its natural habitat is arable fields, gardens, banks, hedgerows, wasteland, logging clearings, loading areas and occasionally shores.<ref name=NatureGate/>

==Traditional use==
''Potentilla recta'' is traditionally used as a tonic in Turkey.<ref name="IJTK">{{cite web|title=''Potentilla recta''|url=http://nopr.niscair.res.in/bitstream/123456789/45065/1/IJTK%2017%284%29%20691-698.pdf|website=Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge|publisher=IJTK|accessdate=30 September 2018}}</ref>
